reason: The text recounts the battle of Israel against Amalek (Exodus 17:8-16), emphasizing the crucial role of Moses, the spiritual and military leader, whose actions directly determine victory. When Moses raises his staff/hand, Israel prevails; when he lowers it, Amalek prevails. The narrative highlights the dependence on leadership, divine authority, and God's power working through the elite figure of Moses, rather than demonstrating that regular people possess superior intelligence. The passage portrays the elite leader as indispensable to victory, suggesting the opposite of the stated claim.
